methods.label: Isolate the common power
methods.explanation:
Both sides contain a power of \(9\), so rewrite the larger power to expose the common quantity. Because the base is positive, the exponent law gives \(9^{x+2}=9^x\cdot9^2=81\cdot9^x\). Hence
\[
81\cdot9^x=240+9^x,
\qquad
80\cdot9^x=240,
\qquad
9^x=3.
\]
Now \(3=\sqrt9=9^{1/2}\). Since \(9>1\), the function \(9^x\) is strictly increasing, so equal powers of this base have equal exponents. Therefore \(x=\tfrac12=\boxed{0.5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Positive-base exponent laws, a linear equation in the common power, and a square-root exponent suffice.
